deep.reconstruction:
Context: §3 'Heuristique de W.M.' (Monsky–Washnitzer), subtitled 'Relations avec mes idées de Gauss-Manin'. Grothendieck wants a heuristic reason why the de Rham-type cohomology of a lift of a variety X_0 over the residue field k of W = W(k) should not depend on the lift. He calls this invariance 'assez surprenant à première vue'.

Setup. Suppose X_0 has a big modular family. That means X_0 is the fibre at a closed point t_0 of a proper smooth morphism f: Y → M, where M is of finite type over S = Spec W, and t_0 lies over the closed point s_0 of S. The diagram shows the cube Y mapping by f to a square M. In M, several curves pass through a point; these are sections. M maps by h to the segment Spec W = S with its closed point marked.

Lifts as sections. Every section g: S → M through t_0 gives a proper smooth lift X_g = Y ×_{M,g} S of X_0 over S.

Base change. Put K^· = Rf_*(Ω^·_{Y/M}), the relative de Rham cohomology complex. In the 'bon cas' (Y smooth over M, f proper), base change in the derived category gives Rf_{g*}(Ω^·_{X_g/S}) ≅ Lg^*(K^·). Taking cohomology, 'du moins modulo torsion', this yields g^*(H^i) → R^i f_{g*}(Ω^·_{X_g/S}) as an isomorphism, where H^i = R^i f_*(Ω^·_{Y/M}). The Tor-terms of the derived pullback are what create the torsion ambiguity.

Next page. For different sections g, g' through t_0 (so g ≡ g' mod p), the pullbacks g^*K^· should be canonically isomorphic, by a transitive system of isomorphisms. Grothendieck interprets this system as a 'stratification' of K^·, and of the H^i, near t_0 relative to S. He then renames it 'descente', which is the crystal idea.

Modern reading:
- The canonical isomorphisms come from the Gauss–Manin connection on H^i_dR(Y/M) relative to S.
- The connection is integrated by the Taylor series Σ (g'−g)^n/n! ∇^n along the p-adic residue disc of t_0.
- This converges because g'−g ∈ pW and pW carries divided powers. That is why one works modulo torsion, or after ⊗Q.
- The faint pencil marginalia (log(k+1), (k±1/2)log) look like Stirling-type estimates for log k!. These are plausibly scratch work for the p-adic size of n!, i.e. convergence of p^n/n!, though this is conjectural.

The page thus motivates crystalline cohomology: independence of the lift is the horizontality/parallel transport of the Gauss–Manin connection over a PD-thickening.
errors: The iso H^i(Lg^*K^·) ≅ g^*H^i(K^·) is not true in general. It needs flatness or vanishing Tor; Grothendieck hedges correctly with 'modulo torsion' and 'bon cas'.
The existence of a smooth proper 'modular' family Y/M through X_0 is a heuristic assumption. Deformations may be obstructed, so it is not guaranteed in general.

The torsion caveat later proved unnecessary in the proper smooth case. Crystalline cohomology (Berthelot) gives integral canonical isomorphisms between the de Rham cohomologies of two lifts, using the divided powers on pW. Strictly this holds for p ≠ 2 or with care, so this is a matter of the heuristic being pessimistic rather than an error.

ideas.what: Independence of the de Rham cohomology of a lift of X_0 from the choice of lift, explained via a modular family and its sections
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline nature of de Rham cohomology / Gauss–Manin parallel transport on residue discs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 IHES lectures, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'), Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), heuristic opening sections

ideas.what: Derived base change Rf_{g*}Ω_{X_g/S} ≅ Lg^* Rf_*Ω_{Y/M}
ideas.modern_name: Base change for relative de Rham cohomology (perfect complexes)

ideas.what: Transitive system of isomorphisms on g^*K^· viewed as a stratification, then renamed 'descente'
ideas.modern_name: Stratification / crystal, equivalent to an integrable connection with convergence on PD-neighbourhoods
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes; Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known heuristic Grothendieck published in his 1966 'Crystals' lectures (Dix exposés). Monsky–Washnitzer invariance is explained via a modular family and the Gauss–Manin connection, leading to stratifications and crystals. Nothing here seems absent from the literature. The Stirling-type marginalia are routine convergence scratch work.
transcription_corrections: 'Il s'ensuit, dans des cas[?] modulo[?] torsion[?]' should probably read 'Il s'ensuit, du moins modulo torsion, que'.
's'exprimant[?] disant[?] par le fait' probably reads 's'exprimant disons par le fait'.
The superscripts '(Σ)' on X_g and f_g appear to be a scratched or overwritten mark rather than a meaningful symbol. Read X_g and f_g: X_g → S.
The arrow label in the diagram is h (h: M → S); in the image it is written with a struck or ornamented letter.
The final displayed isomorphism has the arrow pointing from g^*(H^i) to R^i f_{g*}(Ω^·_{X_g/S}) (written ←~ in the image), which is consistent with the transcription.
